items.stem: Which description matches how a recurrent network reads a sentence?

options.text: It reads one word at a time and rewrites a single fixed-size note after each word.
options.feedback: The note is the hidden state. Each step takes the previous note and the next word and produces a new note.

options.text: It keeps every word and compares each word with all the others.
options.feedback: That describes attention, which is the next panel.

options.text: It reads the whole sentence at once and picks out the keywords.
options.feedback: A recurrent network cannot read ahead. It reads in order.

options.text: It looks each word up in a table of meanings.
options.feedback: There is no table of meanings. The note is a list of numbers that the model updates.

items.stem: Before you try it: the model has read "The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired" and is asked what "it" refers to. Which noun will be stronger on the note?

options.text: Street, because it was read more recently.
options.feedback: Each new word makes the older words weaker, so the later noun is stronger.

options.text: Animal, because it is the subject of the sentence.
options.feedback: The note does not track grammar. It only holds weaker traces of earlier words.

options.text: Both equally, because the sentence is short.
options.feedback: The note fades earlier words at every step, even in a short sentence.

options.text: Neither, because nouns are not stored.
options.feedback: All words are written onto the note. The older ones are weaker.

items.try: Press Read it all and ask, then compare the two bars under Two candidates.

items.stem: You switch the sentence from "too tired" to "too wide", and the model still answers "street". What does this show?

options.text: The answer depends on how recently each noun was read, and the last word has no effect on it.
options.feedback: The note holds street more strongly in both sentences, so the answer is the same. Meaning played no part.

options.text: The model understood that streets can be wide.
options.feedback: The same answer was given for "tired", where street is wrong. A model that used meaning would change its answer.

options.text: The model ran out of memory.
options.feedback: The note is always the same size. It does not run out.

options.text: The model is guessing at random.
options.feedback: The choice is fixed by the strengths on the note, so it is the same every time.

items.stem: An older recurrent model reads a 50-page contract. Which problem should you expect?

options.text: Details from the early pages are weak on the note by the end, and training on large amounts of text is slow because words must be read in order.
options.feedback: These are the two problems this panel describes: distance and order.

options.text: It will refuse to read more than 50 words.
options.feedback: There is no word limit. The weakness is that old content fades.

options.text: It will remember the first page best.
options.feedback: The note keeps the newest words strongest and older words weaker.

options.text: It will read all pages at the same time, which makes it very expensive.
options.feedback: A recurrent model reads in order. Reading everything at once is what attention does.
